summary: Shoshun Hayashidera specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He held a post at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2011) and was a professor at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

Shoson Miyamoto (1893–1983) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Oxford. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo, Komazawa, Toyo, and Waseda, and founded the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies.

Shou-chien Shih (born 1951) works in sinology and history/archaeology. He served as a professor at National Taiwan University from circa 1987 to 2004 and was director of the National Palace Museum from circa 2004 to 2006.

Shoyu Hanayama (1931–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1957). He served as vice president of Musashino University (attested 1976) and chairperson of Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai until 1995.

Shozen Kumoi (1915–2017) studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Otani University and under Erich Frauwallner. He served as professor at Otani University (1948–1981) and Bukkyo University (1982), and also lectured at Kyoto University and the University of Vienna.
Shri Krishna Saksena (born 1897) worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.
Shri Krishna Sharma worked in Indology and linguistics. He founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.

Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar (born 1859) was an Indology scholar. He served at Deccan College as assistant to the professor of Sanskrit (1884), and held posts as professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College and Wilson College, Mumbai.

Shrikant S. Bahulkar is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale. He was chief editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and held posts at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth and Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar (1881–1967) studied Indology and philosophy under K. B. Pathak. He served as professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1907–1927), honorary secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, and general secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference.

Shrivatsa Goswami (born 1950) studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University, where he later taught philosophy and religion. He was a visiting scholar at Harvard University, founded Sri Caitanya Prema Samsthana, and held an attested post at Vrindaban Research Institute.

Shu-Fen Chen specializes in linguistics and Indology. She studied at National Tsing Hua University under Chin-Fa Lien and Hans Henrich Hock, and later served as a professor at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).

Shu-chen Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Karen Christina Lang, Bradley Reed, and Ronald G. Dimberg, and served there as a teaching assistant in 1996.
Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar who held posts as a professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and in the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

Shudo Ishii (born 1943) studied Buddhist studies at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata. He spent his career at Komazawa University advancing from assistant to professor (1971–2014), and also served as acting head of Matsugaoka Bunko.

Shuhong Chang (1904–1994) studied in China and France, including at the École des Beaux-Arts. He taught at Zhejiang University, the Central Academy of Fine Arts, and the National Academy of Art, and long directed the Dunhuang Academy.

Shuichi Kato (1919–2008) studied medicine at the University of Tokyo and also attended the University of Paris. Active in Japanology, history, and philosophy, he held posts at Tokyo, Sophia, British Columbia, Berlin, Brown, Ritsumeikan, and Kyoto Museum for World Peace.
Shuichi Maida (1906–1967) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1928 to 1931 and was a student of Haya Akegarasu.

Shuichi Nara (born 1961) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Keio University and held posts as a full-time researcher at the Eastern Institute and lecturer at Chuo University (attested 2026).

Shuji Takayama is a Buddhist studies scholar. His career includes posts as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (2003) and researcher appointments at Bukkyo University (2003), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (2006), and Musashino University (2006).
